abstract: Monitors benthic disturbance assessments, turbidity silt-curtain deployment protocols, and marine mammal mitigation standards
system_message:
You are Marine environmental officer (ENVIRON). The Marine environmental officer (ENVIRON) oversees benthic disturbance assessments, turbidity silt-curtain deployment protocols, and marine mammal mitigation compliance across candidate offshore seabed trenching spreads.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Marine mammal acoustic observation（MAMMAL）
information_points.content:
ENVIRON-MAMMAL-LHT：The North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread maintains a passive acoustic monitoring radius of 500 m within its pre-trenching acoustic exclusion zone as documented in the marine mammal mitigation protocol sheet.
ENVIRON-MAMMAL-XB5：In accordance with its marine mammal mitigation protocol sheet, the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet establishes a passive acoustic monitoring radius of 1000 m within the pre-trenching acoustic exclusion zone.
ENVIRON-MAMMAL-N3E：Per the marine mammal mitigation protocol sheet, the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet operates with a passive acoustic monitoring radius of 750 m across the pre-trenching acoustic exclusion zone.

information_points.title: Monitors benthic disturbance assessments, turbidity silt-curtain deployment protocols, and marine mammal mitigation standards（ECO）
information_points.content:
ENVIRON-ECO-ETQ：Under Turbidity control standard version Standard Version 2.4, the benthic environmental impact compliance review confirms that the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet has obtained turbidity control protocol approval for the sediment resuspension zone along the cable route.
ENVIRON-ECO-ZE9：Evaluated against Turbidity control standard version Standard Version 2.4, the North Sea Mechanical Trenching Spread does not hold turbidity control protocol approval for the sediment resuspension zone along the cable route.
ENVIRON-ECO-H9W：According to the benthic environmental impact compliance review under Turbidity control standard version Standard Version 2.4, the Celtic Horizon Ploughtrench Fleet has secured turbidity control protocol approval across the sediment resuspension zone along the cable route.
ENVIRON-ECO-JCX：Under Turbidity control standard version Standard Version 3.0, the benthic environmental impact compliance review indicates that the Baltic Subsea Jetting Fleet does not possess turbidity control protocol approval for the sediment resuspension zone along the cable route.
